$schema_note: Cross-language conformance vectors for Rill's money path. Read by `cargo test -p rill-core` and by ts/verify-reference.ts, so the Rust implementation and the TypeScript reference are provably measured against one identical set of expectations rather than two drifting test suites.
$authority_note: These vectors encode INTENDED behavior, taken from the reference implementation's own stated invariant — 'no IEEE-754 value ever touches a token amount' — not from its observed output. A vector the reference fails is a defect in the reference, not a vector to weaken.

decimal_to_base_units.$note: Human decimal string to integer base units. Pure string math; the value is never routed through a float.

accepted.why: one fractional digit under a 6-decimal token
exact precision boundary — one base unit
a token with no fractional part at all
leading zeros in the whole part are tolerated
a value a double cannot represent — 0.1 + 6e-18 collapses to 0.1 in IEEE-754, so this passes only with string math
2^53 + 1: the first integer a double cannot represent exactly

rejected.why: more fractional digits than the token supports — truncating would misreport the amount the caller asked for
one digit past the precision boundary
leading whitespace is not silently trimmed
digit separators are not a decimal number

parse_u64.$note: Fields already denominated in base units — spend amounts, budgets, millisecond timestamps.

rejected.why: a decimal point is not a base-unit integer

deepbook_price.$note: DeepBook converts an order price to base units as price * FLOAT_SCALAR * quote_scalar / base_scalar. The reference computes this with `Math.round(value * ...)` on a JS number, so precision depends on the pool's scalar ratio. Computed exactly, the answer is independent of magnitude.

vectors.pool_shape: DEEP_SUI (base 1e6 / quote 1e9, multiplier 1e12) — listed on BOTH testnet and mainnet
vectors.why: The float product lands one base unit above the exact value. At a 1e12 multiplier the double has no bit left to round correctly, and `Math.round` cannot recover what the multiplication already lost. Reachable today on DEEP_SUI, and on NS_SUI and DRF_SUI on mainnet.
second instance of the same divergence, to show it is systematic rather than a single unlucky value

deepbook_quantity.$note: Order quantity in base units: quantity * base_scalar, exactly. Note the reference computes this as Math.round(value * scalar) on a JS number, so any product above 2^53 (9007199254740992) loses integer precision. At 9 decimals that threshold is reached at roughly 9,007,199 whole units — high for SUI, ordinary for a cheaper 9-decimal token.

vectors.why: Scaled, this exceeds 2^53, so the double cannot represent the integer exactly and the result lands one base unit high. Found by running these vectors against the reference rather than predicted — the price divergence was known first, and this shows the same defect reaches quantity, with no unusual pool shape required.
